topic.title: Devices: worker PCs
topic.shortdesc: Windows PCs running the desktop app take the heavy jobs: ffmpeg video, GPU work and local Claude Code. Link them, give them what their role needs, and watch their jobs.

body.p: Each computer shows whether it is Online, what it can do, when it was last seen and its desktop app version. Unlink stops it taking jobs until you link it again.

ol.li: Choose Download for Windows and run the installer. If Windows warns that it isn't signed, choose More infoRun anyway.
Open the app and sign in with your email and password.
Approve the computer, as below. There is nothing to set up in Railway.

body.p: The app updates itself when it starts. When this page says a new version is available, choose Update now beside it: the computer finishes the job it is running, installs the update and restarts. Older apps don't show Update now; choose Check for updates in their tray menu once.

The desktop app opens this page with a link code. Check the app shows the same code, then choose Link this computer. It connects within seconds. An expired code: choose Link this computer in the app's tray menu to start again.

Each computer lists the roles it can play, such as video rendering, with Ready or how many components are missing. Install … installs them on that computer through winget; Windows may ask there for permission. It waits until the computer is online, and needs App Installer from the Microsoft Store. Some components say Install yourself, with a link.

Each job shows what it needs, which computer has it, and its progress. A queued job says why it is waiting (usually no online computer with that capability) and can be cancelled. A finished video shows a preview; a failed job shows its error with Copy error.
